text.title: API Gateway Patterns & Technology Selection Worked Example
text.summary: One end-to-end worked example showing how api-gateway-patterns produces a valid decision-record artefact.

example.title: Happy-path application
example.code:
--- artefact_id: api-gateway-patterns-acme-2026-05-23 owner: Ruslan Faion <ruslan@faion.net> adr_id: 017 pattern: bff product: kong ---
## Context B2B SaaS with three client families: web admin console, mobile partner app, and webhook receivers. Each family hits 8-12 backend services with different aggregation needs.
## Decision Adopt the BFF pattern with Kong gateways; one BFF per client family backed by a shared Kong cluster.
## Alternatives Rejected | Option | Reason rejected | |--------|-----------------| | envoy | Team has no Envoy operator; managed UX needed for solo founder. | | aws-apigw | Hetzner-hosted backend; cross-cloud egress cost too high. | | per-service | Operational fan-out unsustainable at 12 services with 1.5 ops engineers. |
## Consequences - One additional hop per request (~3-5ms added p95). - Cross-cutting concerns (auth, rate limit, observability) consolidated. - Vendor concentration on Kong — tagged partial_two_way (3 weeks rollback to Traefik).
example.note: Demonstrates the rules from 01-core-rules.xml applied to a concrete input; output validates against the schema in 02-output-contract.xml.

section.title: Operational configuration (procedure steps 6-9)

example.title: gateway_config block honouring r6-r13
example.note: Cascade holds (2000 < 5000 < 10000). Rate limit keyed on the API key, not the CDN's IP.

example.title: Kong declarative route — the four allowed plugins only
example.code: _format_version: "3.0" services: - name: user-service url: http://user-service:8080 routes: - name: users-route paths: [/api/users] strip_path: false preserve_host: true plugins: - name: jwt config: { claims_to_verify: [exp] } - name: rate-limiting config: { minute: 100, policy: redis, limit_by: consumer } - name: correlation-id config: { header_name: X-Request-ID, generator: uuid, echo_downstream: true } - name: cors config: { origins: ["https://app.example.com"], headers: [Authorization, Content-Type] }
example.note: limit_by: consumer satisfies r7; correlation-id at ingress satisfies r8; preserve_host prevents Host header breakage.

example.title: nginx rate limit keyed on the wrong variable
example.note: The bad form is antipattern ip-rate-limit-behind-cdn in 03-failure-modes.xml.

example.title: BFF fan-out with per-service timeout and partial degradation
example.code: async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=2.0) as c: # per-service, not global (r13) user, orders, notifs = await asyncio.gather( c.get("http://user-svc/me", headers=h), c.get("http://order-svc/me/orders?limit=5", headers=h), c.get("http://notify-svc/me/unread", headers=h), return_exceptions=True, ) return { # partial failure degrades, never 500s "user": user.json() if getattr(user, "is_success", False) else None, "orders": orders.json() if getattr(orders, "is_success", False) else [], "notifications": notifs.json() if getattr(notifs, "is_success", False) else [], }
example.note: Parallel fan-out, 2s per hop, null/[] on a failed upstream. No caching in the BFF — that belongs at the gateway (r13).
